  "ledger": [
    "00:00.000–00:06.750, every 0.250-second sample: 4 metal cups; no cup added or removed.",
    "00:07.000–00:08.750, every 0.250-second sample: 4 cups remain distinguishable, with increasing overlap as the camera circles the table.",
    "00:09.000–00:09.125: 4 cup rims remain distinguishable in the closer transition frames; the left pair increasingly overlap.",
    "00:09.250–00:09.750: 3 cups are separately visible; the fourth cup's projected position is behind the left-hand cluster. Occlusion prevents confirming a physical decrease from 4.",
    "00:00.000–00:00.500: manipulated gold coins comprise 1 held upright, 1 visible inside the nearest cup, and at least 2 overlapping disks in the middle cup; concealed contents cannot be counted.",
    "00:00.750–00:02.000: the foreground hand covers the nearest cup and its coin; retain the hidden coin rather than infer disappearance.",
    "00:02.250–00:03.500: 1 coin is visibly lifted from the nearest cup; 2 coins are subsequently distinguishable in the performer's hands. This is a visible transfer, not an increase.",
    "00:03.750–00:06.500: 2 hand-held coins are intermittently visible beside the cups; cup contents become obscured by hands, rims, and the lowering viewpoint.",
    "00:06.750–00:08.500: hand-held coins are intermittently occluded; no reliable total-count change is established.",
    "00:08.750–00:09.750: 1 coin is clearly raised in one hand; the other hand obscures the second coin near the tabletop. No confirmed disappearance or change of object kind.",
    "00:00.000–00:03.500: the pale tabletop area shows 3 large loose coin-like disks, one initially cropped at the bottom, and 2 overlapping small disks. The large disk becoming fully visible is explained by camera movement.",
    "00:03.750–00:07.750: the 3 large loose tabletop disks remain distinguishable when unobstructed; small disks and cup contents become difficult to resolve. No visible pickup of the loose large disks.",
    "00:08.000–00:09.750: cups and hands obscure the previously visible loose tabletop disks as the camera circles; a complete loose-coin count is unavailable, so no disappearance is established.",
    "00:00.000–00:09.750: numerous coin-like border designs cannot reliably be separated into physical objects versus cloth decoration; no defensible count-change finding for this border."
